intent: To compare marijuana usage rates between the United States and the Netherlands, illustrating that the country where it is legal has a lower usage rate.

units.meaning: In the United States, 42% of surveyed people have tried marijuana at least once.

basis.note: Printed table value for US marijuana usage rate.

accepted_routes: 42% of surveyed US people have tried marijuana at least once.
In the United States, 42 percent have tried marijuana.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A US-labeled mark/segment must be visible and labeled with 42% or 42.
units.temporal_anchor: First narration clause: 'Researchers find that 42 % ... in the US ...'
units.reviewer_question: Is the US value of 42% required as an explicit endpoint in the video?

units.meaning: In the Netherlands, 20% of surveyed people have tried marijuana at least once.

basis.note: Printed table value for Netherlands marijuana usage rate.

accepted_routes: 20% of surveyed people in the Netherlands have tried marijuana at least once.
Only 20 percent in the Netherlands have tried marijuana.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A Netherlands-labeled mark/segment must be visible and labeled with 20% or 20.
units.temporal_anchor: Second narration clause: 'In contrast, only 20 % ... in the Netherlands ...'
units.reviewer_question: Is the Netherlands value of 20% required as an explicit endpoint in the video?

units.meaning: The US marijuana usage rate is higher than the Netherlands rate: 42% vs 20%.

basis.note: US endpoint used in the cross-entity comparison.
Netherlands endpoint used in the cross-entity comparison.

accepted_routes: US rate is higher than Netherlands rate: 42% vs 20%.
Netherlands has a lower marijuana usage rate than the US: 20% vs 42%.
US leads the Netherlands in marijuana usage, 42% to 20%.
42% in the US compared with 20% in the Netherlands.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both US and Netherlands marks/segments must appear in the same chart so their order 42 > 20 is visually discernible.
units.temporal_anchor: The 'In contrast' transition after both endpoints are introduced.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly compare the two countries rather than only showing isolated values?

optional_valid: Clarify that percentages are shares of surveyed people, not raw counts.
Use US and Netherlands flag/circle cues to identify the two entities.
Non-causal contextual note that the Netherlands is the lower-usage country; do not state that legal status caused the difference.
unsupported_to_avoid: The 38-year legalization duration, because that number is not in the table.
Causal claims that marijuana legalization caused the lower Netherlands usage rate.
Saying the US rate is 22% higher than the Netherlands; the supported derived difference is 22 percentage points.
Saying the Netherlands rate is exactly half the US rate, because 20/42 ≈ 47.6%, not exactly 50%.
Raw counts such as '42 people' or '20 people' without a survey denominator.
Extrapolating these survey rates to all residents or future years.
notes: Core G1 content is US 42%, Netherlands 20%, and US > Netherlands. The 22-point difference and 2.1x ratio are useful optional derived units; legalization causality and the 38-year figure are not supported by the table.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
